title: ETH AI Center Researchers Community Meetup
venue: ETH AI Center, OAT X 11, Oerlikon
blurb: Recurring meetup series for the AI research community at ETH Zurich.

title: ArtTech Hack 2026
blurb: A three-day hackathon in Zurich for students and recent graduates from art, design and technology, with briefs in data, simulation and robotics — challenges revealed Friday, building Saturday, jury presentations Sunday.

title: Build Your Own Assistant: Never Walk Into A Meeting Blind
blurb: Build an agent that briefs you on the person, the company and the purpose before every meeting, then drafts the follow-up the moment it ends.

title: Zurich Language AI Meetup #22
blurb: Three talks on language AI in Zurich — masking personal data without breaking a language pipeline, benchmarking LLM translations against thousands of native speakers, and a session from Supertext’s CTO — followed by drinks.

title: AI in azienda: Dal prompt al processo
venue: Campus Est USI-SUPSI, Blocco C, Aula C1.02, Via la Santa 1, Viganello
blurb: Second of three Italian-language evenings on using AI deliberately in a business: turning individual tool use into organisational value, with a Use Case Canvas worked through on the spot. Thirty places, priority to local SMEs.

title: Cloudflare Community Meetup #3 — AI Updates Fresh out of Connect San Francisco
blurb: The Swiss Cloudflare user group condenses the AI announcements from Connect San Francisco into one evening, then hands over to community members showing what they have actually built on the platform.

title: AI Agent Sandbox: Could an Agent Help With This?
blurb: Bring a repetitive or awkward task from your own work and the room takes it apart together to see whether an agent would actually help — discussion and experimentation rather than a lecture, with no prior agent experience needed.

title: The Data Stewards Master Class with Stefaan Verhulst
blurb: A limited-places afternoon master class on data stewardship — who holds responsibility for data being shared, and how to organise that in practice — held the day before the Swiss Data Space Forum and closing with a networking apéro.

title: Leading Data Conference Switzerland 2026
cost: 200 CHF (170 early bird) / 140 CHF members (110 early bird)
blurb: DAMA Switzerland's annual data leadership conference at IMD Lausanne, covering data modelling, data-as-an-asset workshops, and CDMP certification.

title: Mapping Knowledge Across Time by Paul Kahn
blurb: Author Paul Kahn compares seven notable visual works from the 12th to the 20th century — their maps, diagrams and illustrations — and draws out what their design choices mean for digital data visualisation today, with a group Q&A to close. Also livestreamed.

title: MS Cloud for IT Pro Zentralschweiz — Podium Special
organiser: MS Cloud for IT Pro Zentralschweiz
blurb: An open-mic German-language panel in Lucerne on how much control a company really keeps in the cloud — data location, the US CLOUD Act, foreign authority access, compliance and exit strategies — with Microsoft Switzerland’s CTO, a CIO, a lawyer and an MVP.

title: Swiss Data Space Forum 2026: Unlocking Data for AI
blurb: National forum on data governance and data spaces for AI, hosted at unlimitrust.

title: AWS Community Day Speakers Session
blurb: Community talks on the original AWS Community Day date, covering how to secure AI agents, spec-driven development with Kiro, cost control on AWS IoT Core and DynamoDB pitfalls, with lunch and networking.

title: CAR16 : IA en entreprise avec AI Foundry et sécurité des MCP
venue: Tesla Store Genève, Rue de la Confédération 8
blurb: French-language Azure community evening in Geneva on enterprise AI with Azure AI Foundry, securing Model Context Protocol servers, and modern cloud architecture and automation with GitHub Copilot.

title: Claude Code Workshop for Beginners
blurb: A two-hour online beginners' session from the Geneva-based Switzerland AI Community on getting started with Claude Code, working through a small project with instructors on hand for the exercises.

title: Cloud-Native Geospatial Zürich
blurb: The closing stop of the Cloud-Native Geospatial Forum's 2026 series, hosted by Meta in Zurich — an afternoon of talks, demos and community for practitioners working on cloud-native formats and pipelines for geospatial data, followed by a reception.

title: Workshop: The Anomaly in Plain Sight
blurb: A hands-on evening on anomalies nobody flagged: how people approach unfamiliar data, feature engineering and machine learning to surface hidden patterns with a look at Polars, why a flagged transaction is not yet fraud, and using generative AI to explain detection results in plain language.

title: Conversation avec Bruno Giussani sur l'emprise et la souveraineté technologique
venue: HEG Bâtiment C Nexus Agora, Rue de la Tambourine 17
blurb: A French-language discussion with Swiss author and podcaster Bruno Giussani on resisting technological capture and European dependence on American digital infrastructure, drawing on his Manuel de résistance à l'emprise technologique.

title: Fabric & Power BI User Group Geneva 2026
blurb: Fifth Romandie gathering of the Swiss Fabric & Power BI user group: MVP Alexandru Badiu on what the new Fabric Apps are good for and what they cost, then the latest news out of FabCon Europe, followed by an apéro.

title: The Great Data Heist: Trust, Power & Cyber Warfare
venue: Uptown Geneva, Rue de la Servette 2
blurb: Cybersecurity experts and hackers unpack how data breaches actually happen, with live hacking demos and an immersive escape game.

title: Robot Learning Paper Club — The RL Post-Training Edition
blurb: Zurich’s robot-learning community — scattered across ETH, big tech and startups — meets for short talks and paper walkthroughs on reinforcement learning for post-training vision-language-action models and world models.

title: Spec-driven Development mit KI
venue: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule, Campus Rapperswil, Oberseestrasse 10
blurb: Two German-language talks on the OST Rapperswil campus: Java Champion Simon Martinelli on driving development from specifications with AI, and Michael Inden on why algorithms and data structures matter more, not less, once everyone can generate code — followed by networking.

title: SURGE 2026: AI. Energy. Robotics.
cost: CHF 499 (early bird sold out; startup discounts available)
blurb: A deliberately small afternoon — roughly 100 to 150 people — on where AI, energy and robotics meet, with keynotes, panels on energy-and-AI and AI-and-robotics, and structured one-to-one sessions for founders, operators and executives. Attendance is by request.

title: AI Breakfast #55 Luzern
blurb: Louis Hermann, co-founder of DocPier, on how accurate document processing actually has to be before it can run in production, why a generic model on its own is not enough, and what trustees, insurers and banks can take from that for their own AI projects.

title: BaselHack 2026
blurb: Free 48-hour hackathon for the Basel region with open and sponsored challenges, for developers, designers and anyone wanting to turn an idea into a working prototype.

title: From Lab to Market: How Can Switzerland Turn World-Class AI Research into World-Class Companies?
blurb: A panel with the presidents and vice-presidents of EPFL and ETH Zurich, GESDA and Proton on the three things Switzerland needs to turn its AI research into companies — compute, capital and data governance — and why the economic value has so far gone elsewhere.

title: KustoCon 2026
cost: EUR 85 in person (workshop, lunch and drinks included) / free online
blurb: A full day on Kusto Query Language at Microsoft’s Zurich Airport campus: a hands-on morning workshop dissecting a real investigation, then an afternoon of practitioner talks on detection engineering and threat hunting, also livestreamed.

title: Ticino Data Conference 2026
venue: Acer EMEA Regional Headquarters, Via della Posta 28
blurb: Free one-day community summit in Ticino with three tracks on Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, AI-assisted tooling and data governance, in English and Italian.

title: Coffee & Prompt #009 (Halloween edition)
blurb: A Halloween edition of the weekly Geneva builders’ coworking morning: bring your own AI project or side hustle, optionally show a feature or a lesson learned, and get feedback from the room.

title: Build Your Own Assistant: What Did I Even Get Done This Week?
blurb: Build an agent that produces daily and weekly recaps of your own or your team's work, alongside the industry and regulatory news that actually affects you.

title: AI and Responsible Business Conduct
organiser: SECO / Federal Department of Foreign Affairs
blurb: A plenary session at the Swiss Forum on Business and Human Rights on applying the UN Guiding Principles and OECD Guidelines to AI systems in practice, with UN representatives, technology companies and civil society. Interpretation in German, French and English.

title: Architecting for Trust: Resilience & Sovereignty on AWS
organiser: Containers and AWS Meetup Group / copebit
blurb: An afternoon hands-on lab on AWS resilience with the Karpenter autoscaler, then an evening of talks from AWS and copebit on designing resilient workloads, running enterprise Claude Code on AWS, and digital sovereignty — closing with pizza and beer.

title: GFN AI Day
cost: CHF 15 members / CHF 70 external (lunch and apéro included)
blurb: A working day rather than a talking one: a morning of practitioner talks from SSF, ZHAW, Correntics and Resilens on what AI can actually do for sustainable finance, then small groups spend the afternoon on real challenges submitted by GFN startups and demo what they built. Thirty places.

title: ISA Lunch & Learn: AI Tools at Work
blurb: A 45-minute English-language lunch session on where AI tools genuinely lift productivity at work, built around real use cases and what has changed recently, closing with open Q&A.

title: Destination AI – Verpasse den Zug nicht!
blurb: Full-day German-language AI conference for the Swiss partner and reseller ecosystem, with a keynote by futurist Gerd Leonhard, vendor breakout sessions and business meetings.

title: Tufa Talks #5 — Dominique Paul (Dream Machines)
blurb: Dream Machines founder Dominique Paul on teaching robots by demonstration so that non-roboticists can automate variable, repetitive manufacturing work in small and medium-sized businesses, followed by Q&A and pizza.

title: Zwischen Prompt und Urteilskraft
organiser: HSLU Institut für Kommunikation und Marketing (IKM) / ZSPR
blurb: Impulse talks and a panel at HSLU Lucerne on what communication work is still worth when AI writes the first draft, and which skills matter next — apéro afterwards.

title: Mindstone Zurich November AI Meetup
blurb: The Zurich edition of the Mindstone AI evenings, hosted at Unit8: a technical demo of what one team learned building a product with LLMs, a practical session on closing the AI skills gap for non-technical students, and a talk on where AI takes work and society next, then pizza and networking.

title: Agentic AI: Wie agentische KI Prozesse übernimmt
blurb: Free German-language webinar with live demos on production systems showing what AI agents can really do today, where they fail, and how to run a safe pilot.

title: AI im Unternehmen: Wo anfangen?
blurb: Free 45-minute German-language webinar in which NETNODE founder Lukas Fischer shows how to find and score AI use cases by value, effort and risk, with three Swiss examples and Q&A.

title: EQS Connect Zurich 2026 — From Compliance Activity to Compliance Impact
cost: Not listed (register interest; places strictly limited)
blurb: An English-language afternoon for compliance, legal and data leaders built entirely around AI: an opening keynote on what AI is doing to judgement, a keynote on Swiss exposure to international AI governance expectations, panels on shadow AI and defensible decisions, and a workshop on where the human–AI boundary should sit.

title: Zürich — 88th Fabric User Group (online)
blurb: The Swiss Fabric user group’s monthly online session: the latest Fabric news, then Franco on automating semantic model health checks with a Fabric notebook, the Best Practice Analyzer, Memory Analyzer and DAX INFO views, writing results to a Lakehouse to track model quality and memory over time.

title: GDG Cloud Zürich: Tech Talks #38
blurb: Two evening talks on Google Cloud and Google DeepMind at Google’s Zurich office, followed by a sponsored apéro — note that doors close at 17:55 and late entry is not possible.

title: Snowflake Forum Zurich 2026
venue: The Circle Convention Center, The Circle 27
blurb: Free data-platform conference bringing together Swiss data teams and partners.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Biomedicine Forum 2026
blurb: A free day in Lugano on AI from basic research through to the clinic: one session on digital twins and personalised medicine, one on protein and compound design, plus abstract talks, posters and a closing conversation on global AI governance ahead of the Geneva AI Summit 2027.

title: HerImpact 2026: Who Decides — You or AI?
blurb: Talks and a panel on who stays accountable when AI shapes an organisational decision — who can question it, correct it or stop it — drawing on current Swiss and Japanese research and real cases, closing with questions the group puts forward for the 2027 Geneva summit.

title: Swiss AI Safety Days 2026
blurb: Two days at ETH Zurich on AI safety research, governance and careers, with trust-based pricing from free upwards. Attendance is by application; the deadline is 17 October.

title: Build Your Own Assistant: Time to Stop AI Slop
blurb: A session on getting an assistant to write in your own voice rather than generic model output, then turning the week's news into a post and a newsletter worth reading.

title: UNIGE – Recherche documentaire et IA
blurb: University of Geneva workshop on using AI tools for academic research.

title: Agentic Trio
blurb: INNOQ’s Fabian Walther reframes Teresa Torres’ Product Trio as an "Agentic Trio", arguing that AI should change how software teams split responsibility — not just how fast they ship.

title: AI in Food — State of Play
organiser: Swiss Food & Nutrition Valley / Porsche Consulting
blurb: A full day of keynotes and workshops for food-industry professionals past the AI hype stage, on what it actually takes to implement AI against real problems inside their own organisations.

title: Apertus for NGOs: Running and Deploying Switzerland’s Open-source LLM
organiser: Swiss AI Initiative (ETH Zurich, EPFL & CSCS)
blurb: Hands-on morning for non-profit staff and researchers on deploying Apertus, Switzerland’s fully open large language model, on their own infrastructure or via a provider — with a Swiss non-profit case study and group exercises.

title: C4DT Conference on AI Sovereignty: Charting Switzerland’s Path
blurb: A full day on how Switzerland builds strategic independence in AI between US and Chinese dominance — lessons from other middle powers, Swiss research including the Apertus foundation model, industry deployment realities, and concrete recommendations for national strategy.

title: Navigating Data Protection and Transfer Impact Assessments for AI Startups
blurb: Breakfast session with lawyers from Wenger Vieli on when a Transfer Impact Assessment is actually required for cross-border data transfers, and how to keep them manageable as an AI company.

title: DevOps for Fabric — Git & Deployment Pipelines
organiser: Data and AI for Intelligent Cloud
blurb: Bringing proper CI/CD to Microsoft Fabric: Git integration, deployment pipelines, variable libraries and sensitivity labels for enterprise-ready BI.

title: Machine Intelligence Summit
cost: Not listed (curated attendance, host approval required)
blurb: Three hundred people who build frontier AI in Europe, across four 80-minute blocks — infrastructure, learning, agents and the physical world — each pairing academia, a frontier lab and a startup, plus founder lightning talks and fifty students presenting posters. Nothing is recorded.

title: MUG Zürich — How to Truly Stop AI Hallucinations
blurb: Two talks from Helvetia Insurance engineers: why factual errors in generative AI apps usually come from weak retrieval design rather than the model — covering semantic chunking, metadata filtering, hybrid search, reranking and output guardrails — and a second session on the benefits and risks of AI-assisted development.

title: Rethinking Architecture Through Residuality and AI
organiser: Software Architecture and Project Design Zurich
blurb: Barry O’Reilly’s Residuality Theory applied to the age of AI-generated code: what architects should still decide themselves when machines write the implementation. Live stream plus a few on-site seats at ERNI.

title: Inside ETH Zurich’s Data Stack: Analytics for Universities
blurb: A walk through a real analytics stack built with ETH Zurich — the original setup and why, what got bolted on later, how individual departments were brought up to speed with the data, and where it goes next — then open discussion over drinks.

title: IKM Impuls: Vom Trigger zum Agenten
organiser: HSLU Institut für Kommunikation und Marketing (IKM)
blurb: Lunchtime session from HSLU on what changes when marketing automation stops following rules and starts deciding, and what companies need in data, technology and organisation to run AI agents in customer dialogue.

title: Swiss Data & AI — AI Enabled Workflows
organiser: Swiss Data and AI Group (Databricks User Group)
blurb: The first Zurich gathering of the Swiss Data & AI group, on automating data work with AI-enabled workflows. Topics, speakers and the venue are still to be announced, and the group is open to offers to speak.

title: AI Startup Center Community Meetup — November Edition
blurb: A deliberately informal morning meetup over coffee for the centre’s AI startups and corporate partners — no agenda and no presentations, just conversations about partnerships, where AI is heading and what is actually hard right now.

title: Business Leaders' Evening: Your AI, your data, under your roof
venue: LeBooster Genève, Route de Jussy 35 (2nd floor)
organiser: ABAXINFO / AXION / Keeping Life Simple, hosted by CCI France Suisse
blurb: A French-language evening for SME leaders on getting value from AI without giving up control of the data: three levels of sovereign AI, a live demo of a fully offline model answering on a sample company’s documents with per-employee permissions, what the revised Swiss data protection act expects of management, and a networking apéro.

title: IA : meetup « Generative AI Genève » #5
blurb: Your data, your models, your infrastructure: ELCA and EPFL spin-off Anyway Systems on running LLMs locally or in a private cloud, and on the trade-offs between performance, sovereignty and cost when a company wants generative AI without handing over its data.

title: SC71: Meetup Database / PostgreSQL
venue: Swissquote Bank SA, Chemin de la Crétaux 33
blurb: Two database talks hosted by Swissquote in Gland — PostgreSQL on Kubernetes with Laurent Parodi and multi-version concurrency control with Louis Tochon — followed by a quiz and apéro.

title: AI Futures: Trajectories for a Post-AGI Civilization
venue: ETH Zurich Main Building, Rämistrasse 101, Room F 26.5
blurb: Part of a discussion series on where AI development leads: expert forecasts for transformative AI, the economic effects of AGI, possible civilisational paths and what to do about them, mixing short explainers with group discussion.

title: Swiss Robotics Day 2026
organiser: ETH Zurich RobotX / Swiss Robotics Association
blurb: The national robotics meeting point: keynotes, panels and workshops alongside an exhibition floor with 60+ exhibitors and live demos, bringing together labs, industry, policymakers and spin-offs.

title: Hype vs. Shipped: What AI Really Changes in Product Work
blurb: Two talks on what AI has actually changed in building products: Coople on a year spent replacing squads, sprints and story points with AI-first workflows and smaller teams, including the experiments that failed, and Brack.Alltron on where AI earned its place and why plain analytics sometimes still beats machine learning.

title: Swiss AI Summit 2026
cost: CHF 790 Executive Pass / CHF 950 standard (excl. VAT)
blurb: Full-day summit at the Kunsthaus for senior business, technology and government leaders, spanning finance and insurance, government and defence, manufacturing, cybersecurity, quantum and healthcare — with speakers from Microsoft Switzerland, IBM, Nestlé, ABB, HSBC and the Canton of Zurich, plus workshops, demos and a one-to-one meeting platform.

title: AI in azienda: AI sotto controllo
venue: Campus Est USI-SUPSI, Blocco C, Aula C1.02, Via la Santa 1, Viganello
blurb: Closing evening of the Ticino series on conscious AI use in business, this one on data, responsibility, rules and governance — content, a hands-on workshop and networking, capped at thirty participants.

title: Growing Together Conference GTC26
venue: The Circle Convention Center, The Circle 27
blurb: A full day for business and data leaders on getting AI past isolated use cases and into scalable capability — keynotes from Benedict Evans and Google Cloud’s Alon Halevy, leader tracks with Helvetia, Axpo and Emmi, plus tech talks and workshops.

title: AI in Production: Introduction to MLOps — Training at EPFL
cost: CHF 1,000 (10% off for EPFL alumni and SDSC partners)
blurb: One-day SDSC training on designing, deploying and operating ML systems at scale — version control, CI/CD, experiment tracking, monitoring, drift detection and automated retraining. Registration closes 24 September.

title: Satellite Event: From Data to Decisions — AI in Asset Management
blurb: A Swiss AI Summit satellite session on how asset managers turn increasingly complex data into usable investment insight, and where AI makes a genuine difference rather than noise.

title: Satellite Event: From Smart AI to Better Work
blurb: An interactive executive lab run with Zeix on redesigning work around AI: deciding what the machine should actually do, and marking out where human judgement, responsibility and control have to stay.

title: DINAcon 2026
blurb: Switzerland’s conference on digital sustainability — 36 sessions on open source, open data, digital sovereignty, data protection and copyright, with 250+ attendees and a closing Hacknight.

title: AI Risks in CyberSecurity
venue: Novotel Genève Centre, Rue de Zurich 19
blurb: Afternoon session in Geneva on how organisations can keep using AI internally without taking on unmanaged risk, with presentations followed by a networking reception; CPE credits available via ISC2 and ISACA.

title: Agentic Engineering Days Zurich 2026
blurb: A one-day engineering conference on AI coding and agent systems: 38+ sessions across four tracks — using AI tools, building AI-powered systems, sponsor spotlights and hands-on workshops — with speakers from OpenAI, Hugging Face, NVIDIA, Google and AWS.

title: AI Breakfast #56 Luzern
blurb: Merun Gugelmann of Aeberli Treuhand on how an 80-year-old trust company got from Microsoft Teams to building its own Azure applications — the steps of that digitisation journey, concrete examples, and the setup on Azure App Services.

title: STEM4Health Hackathon
venue: ETH Zürich Campus Hönggerberg, HPH building
organiser: Johnson & Johnson Switzerland / Swiss Data Science Center
blurb: A hundred students and early-career researchers spend a weekend on real pharmaceutical manufacturing problems, combining manufacturing data, mechanistic modelling and machine learning with industry and academic mentors before pitching to a jury.

title: AI Safety: Building Trustworthy AI in the Real World
organiser: Elevate Tech: Women and Minorities in AI, Tech, and Science
blurb: Four speakers from Google, AWS, Unique and Systematic-X on keeping AI systems trustworthy once they act on their own — how to evaluate and monitor before and after deployment, where guardrails, human oversight and red-teaming fit, and how to ship fast without losing accountability.

title: KI-Agenten & -Work: Skills und Anbindungen für konkrete Entlastung im Alltag
blurb: A full German-language day with Michael Kyburz on getting AI to take over recurring work: three base skills, how to build your own, and wiring assistants into calendar, mail and project tools so multi-step workflows run with clear checkpoints for human review. Fifteen places, and a paid ChatGPT or Claude subscription is required.

title: The Geneva AI Conference 2026
blurb: An evening on enterprise AI strategy and returns, opened by Geneva city executive councillor Joëlle Bertossa and built around a panel with IBM, SAP, Hostelworld and Executive AI. The venue is still to be confirmed.

title: Mindstone Geneva November AI Meetup
venue: L’Annexe by Rentes Genevoises, Rue du Port 3
blurb: Monthly Geneva AI evening with three practical talks — building with LLMs, working faster with AI and where it is all heading — then pizza and networking. Forty places.

title: After Microsoft Ignite Special 2026
organiser: Swiss Microsoft Community (Microsoft Cloud Security & Modern Work)
blurb: Swiss MVPs recap the announcements from Microsoft Ignite 2026 in short sessions on Cloud & AI, the agent platform, Copilot and Microsoft IQ, security, data security and compliance, and agentic business applications, with an apéro after.

title: Hack Apertus — Onsite Hackathon Zurich
blurb: The on-site leg of the national Apertus hackathon: build on the open Apertus 8B model, strengthen its multilingual abilities and ship applications for private- and public-sector problems, with everything released as Open Commons.

title: AI Insights for Chief Executives
venue: Swiss AI Tower, ETH Zürich, Andreasstrasse 5
blurb: Executive workshop for CEOs, CFOs, CDOs and CTOs on turning data and AI into measurable business value, with case studies from EKZ, Merck and Richemont. Limited seats.

title: Databricks Data + AI World Tour Zurich 2026
blurb: Databricks' flagship Swiss stop on the Data + AI World Tour: keynotes, breakout sessions and hands-on training on Genie and Lakebase, plus an expo, with speakers from Databricks and Zurich Insurance.

title: Reshaping Information Research with AI
blurb: Two-hour on-site workshop from the EPFL Library comparing four AI-powered research assistants, how they work and where they differ from traditional information retrieval. Open to the public, registration required.

title: IBM Bob Coding Watch Party Zürich — Final Edition
blurb: The closing session of IBM's 2026 hybrid series on IBM Bob, its AI development assistant — coding live alongside other European cities, with beginner, intermediate and expert tracks covering everything from first idea to modernising legacy applications.

title: KI-Strategie und -Governance für KMUs
blurb: A 90-minute German-language session for SME decision-makers on steering generative AI use rather than letting it spread: setting a strategic frame, drafting an internal AI policy, weighing data-protection, liability and wrong-output risks, and planning a safe rollout under Swiss data protection law and the EU AI Act. Fifteen places.

title: Ein Team, ein Plan und viele Agenten
blurb: A German-language breakfast session with Quatico CEO Jan Wloka on why adding more AI agents tends to produce more review work than finished work, and the three changes that fixed it for his team: a written decision before any agent starts coding, work split into packages that run in parallel, and one daily overview of what needs a human. Aimed at product owners and delivery leads, with a real work package run live.

title: Swiss IT Minds 2026 — IT, AI & Cyber Security
cost: Not listed (complimentary participation for qualified attendees)
blurb: Two days for Swiss IT and data leaders at the Dolder Grand on enterprise AI as a strategic capability, centralised versus decentralised AI governance in large organisations, securing AI agents as a hybrid workforce, and the governance basics behind all of it.

title: dbt Meetup Zurich
blurb: Evening for the Zürich dbt community aimed at analytics engineers, data engineers and data leaders, opening with Massimo Turola of Bank Vontobel on using dbt to manage Snowflake Cortex AI applications in an AI data catalog, then an apéro.

title: Hack Apertus — Onsite Hackathon Basel
blurb: The Basel leg of the national Apertus hackathon series, building applications and multilingual improvements on Switzerland’s open Apertus model, with everything produced released for reuse. Venue still to be announced.

title: Christmas Special Hackathon — Operation Silent Night
blurb: Festive team hackathon where the Zurich Databricks User Group turns a sabotage mystery into hands-on practice with Genie, Lakebase and Databricks Apps.

title: Azure Zurich User Group X-Mas Special 2026
blurb: The Azure Zürich User Group closes the year with its Christmas get-together at Frau Gerolds Wintergarten — no agenda, just food, glühwein and the Swiss Azure community. Places are limited.

title: KubeVirt in Practice & AI in QA: What Works, What Doesn't
blurb: Two talks in Zurich: Red Hat's Simon Krenger on running virtual machines next to containers with KubeVirt, including live demos and when it is the wrong tool, and Basia Karaagac on where AI genuinely helps in QA and where exploratory testing and human risk judgement still win.

title: Fabric Year in Review 2026 — Highlights & Outlook
organiser: Data and AI for Intelligent Cloud
blurb: Year-end session from the Zurich Microsoft data-platform group on what actually shipped in Fabric during 2026 and what is worth planning for next.

title: The Night of Data Talents: Startup Edition
blurb: Swiss data startups pitch to an investor panel with community voting, capping the year for the Suisse Romande data scene.

title: digitalswitzerland @ Davos
blurb: A full day in Davos on Switzerland's digital future, with speakers from business, government and research building on the national AI Action Plan and looking ahead to the Geneva AI Summit 2027. Programme details still to be published.

title: Digital Lounge @ Davos — Enterprise Data, AI & Robotics
blurb: An invitation-only forum during Davos week for CxOs and transformation leaders on enterprise data, AI and robotics — morning and afternoon keynotes and panels, a live technology showcase, entrepreneur talks and parallel workshops, closing with an awards ceremony and dinner.

title: AI for Decision Makers — Executive Course at ETH Zurich
time: 09:00–17:00 on 22, 28 and 29 January and 4 and 5 February
organiser: Swiss Data Science Center / ETH Zürich School for Continuing Education
cost: CHF 4,000 (10% off for ETH staff and alumni and SDSC partners)
blurb: A five-day English-language executive course for leaders who need to challenge assumptions on AI projects without becoming data scientists — data science foundations, MLOps, AI governance and ethics, generative AI and a first agent, with an ETH Zurich certificate. Registration closes 15 January 2027.

title: Generative AI & Agentische Systeme
organiser: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule (Institut für Computational Engineering)
blurb: Two-day German-language course for developers, architects, data scientists and ML engineers on building agentic LLM systems that survive production: function calling, hybrid-search RAG, LangGraph topologies, security hardening and systematic evaluation. Places are limited.

title: SWAT4HCLS 2027
blurb: The 15th edition of the long-running international conference on semantics in healthcare and life sciences — ontologies, knowledge graphs and AI — with keynotes, tutorials and a dedicated biohackathon day in Basel.

title: SDSC-Connect: Connecting Digital Environmental Sciences
venue: Central Bern venue to be announced
blurb: A day in Bern on making environmental data usable across disciplines and institutions — data access and sharing, data infrastructure, and the role of machine learning and AI across climate, ecology, hydrology, the cryosphere, natural hazards and agriculture, with keynotes, invited talks, break-outs and a poster fair. Seats are limited and the venue is still to be announced.

title: AI & Quantum Course: From Foundations to Scalable Intelligence
blurb: An afternoon course run with Quantum Basel, led by its CTO Jan Mikolon, bridging current AI practice and quantum technologies — from the foundations through to what it takes to scale.

title: Kickstart AI Workflows with Databricks
organiser: Swiss Data & AI Group (Databricks User Group)
blurb: Hybrid Databricks user-group evening in Zurich on automating data work with AI-enabled workflows, including a session on Databricks Apps and Lakebase applied to clinical cancer research cohorts. Rescheduled from November 2026 to February 2027.

title: AI Days 2027 — Geneva
blurb: Geneva leg of the fifth AI Days, the Swiss AI Center’s applied-AI conference for SMEs, with workshops, talks, research and demos. Registration not yet open.

title: AI Days 2027 — Yverdon-les-Bains
blurb: Yverdon-les-Bains leg of AI Days 2027, the Swiss AI Center’s applied-AI conference for SMEs, with workshops, talks and demos. Registration not yet open.

title: AI Days 2027 — Fribourg
blurb: Fribourg leg of AI Days 2027, the Swiss AI Center’s applied-AI conference for SMEs, closing the three-city edition with workshops, talks and demos. Registration not yet open.
